_note: Sources for Form 2 Chemistry (Batch C2-1, Term 1). Computed answers follow the rules and tables named here.

atomic-structure.ref: Dalton's atomic theory (1803-1808); protons, neutrons and electrons; Bohr's model with shells of 2, 8, 8 for the first 20 elements; atomic number, mass number, isotopes
atomic-structure.supports: The statements of Dalton's theory and its later corrections; particle charges and masses; electron arrangements; neutrons = mass number − atomic number. Mass numbers used: the most common isotope of each of the first 20 elements (Cl 35).
atomic-structure.checked: Standard results; arrangements and particle numbers computed by code (science2.js, tested). The mass-number table is authored: please check it.

symbols-valency.ref: Chemical symbols (IUPAC), valencies of common elements and radicals, writing formulae by swapping valencies, naming binary compounds (-ide) and compounds with radicals
symbols-valency.supports: Symbols including those from Latin; radicals OH, NO₃, HCO₃, SO₄, CO₃, PO₄, NH₄ with their valencies; formulae and names built from the valency table.
symbols-valency.checked: Formulae and names computed by code from the authored valency table (science2.js): please check the table (copper given valency 2).

periodic-table.ref: History of the periodic table (Döbereiner 1829, Newlands 1864, Mendeleev 1869, Moseley 1913); groups and periods; the families alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases; trends in reactivity
periodic-table.supports: Group = outer electrons, period = shells; family names and properties; alkali metals more reactive down the group, halogens less reactive; halogen displacement.
periodic-table.checked: Standard results, dates from general knowledge (not opened in this session): please check them.
